OnTick pattern: adopted the SOP Intraday Discipline OnTick (Strategy_EntrySignal runs PER TICK reading cached D1/M15/H1 state) instead of the closed-bar-gated skeleton default, because the card entry is an intrabar tick-level touch of L1/H1. Caches advance on independent QM_IsNewBar(sym,tf) latches (D1 pivots, M15 gate, H1 soft-exit); management + exits run every tick; only NEW entries are gated by spread/news.

Opposite-pivot soft exit direction: card tertiary exit reads literally 'long stopped if an hourly bar closes > H2; short stopped if close < L2' -- geometrically a favorable-overshoot exit (price ran past the mid pivot P to the far inner band), not an adverse stop. Implemented literally per HR9 (most-literal reading); reviewer to confirm intent vs the 'soft exit before hard SL' framing.

TP = pivot P geometry: on days where the prior close sits high in the prior range, P=(H+L+C)/3 can fall BELOW L1 (the long entry) or ABOVE H1 (the short entry). Such entries are skipped (a TP on the wrong side of entry is an invalid order); this is faithful to 'TP at P' and self-consistent with mean-reversion (longs mostly fire on down-close days where P>L1), but it reduces trade frequency on strong-close days. Reviewer to confirm skip vs an alternative fallback TP.

Broker-time native: the Camarilla day boundary (D1 bar rollover == broker 00:00), the 06:00-18:00 entry window, and the 21:00 EOD flatten all use server time (TimeCurrent), which IS DXZ NY-Close broker time -- so no QM_BrokerToUTC/QM_UTCToBroker/QM_IsUSDSTUTC conversion is needed and no DST offset bug class is introduced.
